title: Memory on Trial: A Simulated Investigation into Testimony
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听录音（或阅读文字稿），然后完成10道听力题。听力中包含说话者之间的自然打断、修正和干扰信息，请仔细辨别。之后学习语法规则（复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点），并完成8道语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Maya: So, Daniel, you're running this memory and testimony study. What exactly are you testing?
Daniel: We want to know how confident witnesses are, and how accurate they are. Are they the same thing?
Maya: Good question. What have you found so far?
Daniel: Well, in our first session, we showed people a short video of a bicycle theft. Then we asked them to describe the thief.
Maya: And did they remember well?
Daniel: Some did, some didn't. But here's the interesting part: the people who were most confident were not always the most accurate.
Maya: That's a bit worrying. So confidence is not a reliable guide?
Daniel: Exactly. Although confident witnesses sound convincing, their memories can still be wrong.
Maya: What about the way you ask questions? Does that matter?
Daniel: It matters a lot. If you ask a leading question, you can change what people remember.
Maya: Can you give an example?
Daniel: Sure. We asked one group, "How fast was the car going when it hit the tree?" And another group, "How fast was the car going when it smashed into the tree?"
Maya: And the second group remembered higher speeds?
Daniel: Yes, they did. The word "smashed" made them think the car was faster.
Maya: So the question itself can create a false memory?
Daniel: It can influence memory, yes. Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears, it fills in gaps.
Maya: That's fascinating. But surely some memories are very strong?
Daniel: Of course. Some memories are strong and accurate. But even strong memories can be wrong.
Maya: What about the police? Do they use your findings?
Daniel: Some do. We run training sessions for officers. We tell them to use open questions, not leading ones.
Maya: And do they listen?
Daniel: Mostly, yes. But change is slow. Even though the evidence is clear, some officers still use the old methods.
Maya: I see. So what's your main message?
Daniel: My main message is this: memory is not a video recording. It's more like a story we rebuild each time we remember it.
Maya: That's a powerful way to put it. Thank you, Daniel.
Daniel: Thank you, Maya.

grammar.title: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点
grammar.explanation: 英语句子可以很简单，也可以很复杂。简单句只包含一个主谓结构，例如 'Memory is not a video recording.' 复合句则把两个或更多意思用连接词组合起来。条件用 if 引导，表示“如果……就……”；让步用 although / even though 引导，表示“虽然……但是……”；原因用 because 引导，表示“因为……”。注意：although 和 because 不能和 so 或 but 同时使用。标点方面，复合句的两个部分之间通常用逗号隔开，尤其是当从句在前时，例如 'Although confident witnesses sound convincing, their memories can still be wrong.' 如果主句在前，逗号常可省略。
grammar.example: Although confident witnesses sound convincing, their memories can still be wrong.

options: If you ask a leading question, you can change what people remember.
If you ask a leading question you can change what people remember.
If you ask a leading question, so you can change what people remember.
If you ask a leading question, but you can change what people remember.
answers: If you ask a leading question, you can change what people remember.
questions.explanation: 条件句 if 从句在前时，后面主句前通常加逗号；且 if 从句不能与 so 或 but 连用。
questions.evidence: If you ask a leading question, you can change what people remember.

options: Although confident witnesses sound convincing, their memories can still be wrong.
Although confident witnesses sound convincing, but their memories can still be wrong.
Although confident witnesses sound convincing so their memories can still be wrong.
Although confident witnesses sound convincing their memories can still be wrong.
answers: Although confident witnesses sound convincing, their memories can still be wrong.
questions.explanation: although 引导让步状语从句，不能与 but 或 so 连用；从句在前时，主句前加逗号。
questions.evidence: Although confident witnesses sound convincing, their memories can still be wrong.

options: Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears, it fills in gaps.
Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears, so it fills in gaps.
Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears it fills in gaps.
Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears, but it fills in gaps.
answers: Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears, it fills in gaps.
questions.explanation: because 引导原因状语从句，不能与 so 或 but 连用；从句在前时，主句前加逗号。
questions.evidence: Because the brain tries to make sense of what it hears, it fills in gaps.

options: Even though the evidence is clear, some officers still use the old methods.
Even though the evidence is clear, but some officers still use the old methods.
Even though the evidence is clear so some officers still use the old methods.
Even though the evidence is clear some officers still use the old methods.
answers: Even though the evidence is clear, some officers still use the old methods.
questions.explanation: even though 引导让步状语从句，不能与 but 或 so 连用；从句在前时，主句前加逗号。
questions.evidence: Even though the evidence is clear, some officers still use the old methods.

options: The word "smashed" made them think the car was faster.
The word smashed made them think the car was faster.
The word "smashed" made them think, the car was faster.
The word "smashed" made them think the car was faster,
answers: The word "smashed" made them think the car was faster.
questions.explanation: 引用单词时用引号；句子结尾用句号，且 think 后接宾语从句时不用逗号。
questions.evidence: The word "smashed" made them think the car was faster.

options: Memory is not a video recording; it is like a story we rebuild.
Memory is not a video recording, it is like a story we rebuild.
Memory is not a video recording but it is like a story we rebuild.
Memory is not a video recording so it is like a story we rebuild.
answers: Memory is not a video recording; it is like a story we rebuild.
questions.explanation: 两个独立分句之间可以用分号连接；不能用逗号连接两个独立分句（逗号粘连），也不能随意加 but 或 so。
questions.evidence: Memory is not a video recording; it is like a story we rebuild.

options: We tell them to use open questions, not leading ones.
We tell them to use open questions not leading ones.
We tell them to use open questions, not leading ones,
We tell them to use open questions; not leading ones.
answers: We tell them to use open questions, not leading ones.
questions.explanation: 用逗号分隔对比成分，句子结尾用句号；分号用于连接独立分句，此处不适用。
questions.evidence: We tell them to use open questions, not leading ones.

options: Some memories are strong and accurate, but even strong memories can be wrong.
Some memories are strong and accurate, even strong memories can be wrong.
Some memories are strong and accurate but, even strong memories can be wrong.
Some memories are strong and accurate; but even strong memories can be wrong.
answers: Some memories are strong and accurate, but even strong memories can be wrong.
questions.explanation: 用 but 连接两个独立分句时，前面加逗号；不能只用逗号连接两个独立分句，也不能在 but 后加逗号。
questions.evidence: Some memories are strong and accurate, but even strong memories can be wrong.
